flags.why: The standalone word denotes a king's ceremonial headdress, rather than any decorative crown ([dictionary](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-mi%E1%BB%87n)).
The bride's accessory does not illustrate the royal ceremonial meaning of miện.
flags.fix: Nhà vua đội miện khi tế lễ. = The king wore his ceremonial headdress when performing the rites.

flags.why: Cao ráo describes a person's tall stature and does not mean good-looking or neat.
The obsolete room sense refers to a hotel room, not a generic small chamber ([dictionary](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-s%C4%83m)).
The example presents săm as an ordinary literary word for a private chamber rather than its obsolete hotel-room sense.
flags.fix: Anh ấy thuê một săm trong khách sạn. = He rented a room in the hotel.

flags.why: Phay does not mean chopping or splitting a log; its cutting sense is machining with a milling cutter ([dictionary](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-phay)).
flags.fix: to mill (machine a surface or groove with a rotating cutter)

flags.why: A native speaker would not use phay for splitting firewood in this sentence.
flags.fix: Người thợ phay một rãnh trên chi tiết kim loại. = The worker milled a groove in the metal component.

flags.why: Mô thức belongs to formal or academic usage and needs a register warning for learners.
